evals.prompt: Update page 42 in BookStack to add a new tag Reviewed without overwriting its existing tags or breaking its WYSIWYG formatting.
evals.expected_output: Reads page 42 first (for existing tags and format: raw if editing HTML), then calls update_page with the full combined tags list and without passing rendered html.
assertions: Reads existing page/tags before calling update_page
Preserves existing tags by sending the complete combined tags array (or notes that tags replaces the entire list)
Uses format: raw (not rendered html) if reading/updating WYSIWYG source, or omits html/markdown for a tag-only update

evals.prompt: Find all pages in BookStack updated by user ID 7 and read the full text of a 90,000-character runbook page.
evals.expected_output: Notes that author filters require a user slug or me (not numeric ID 7), uses find_users or asks for slug, and paginates get_page using content_next_offset until null.
assertions: States that BookStack author search filters reject numeric user IDs and require a user slug or me
Mentions find_users (or admin slug lookup) to resolve the user slug
Uses get_page with content_next_offset pagination until content_next_offset is null

evals.prompt: Upload an architecture diagram PNG to BookStack page 42 and embed it in the page, then explain why create_page isn't showing up in my MCP client.
evals.expected_output: Explains create_image uploads the image and returns markdown/html snippets that must be inserted via a separate update_page call, and that write tools are hidden unless BOOKSTACK_ENABLE_WRITE=true.
assertions: Uses create_image and notes a separate update_page call is required to insert the returned snippet
Explains that bookstack-mcp is read-only by default and requires BOOKSTACK_ENABLE_WRITE=true to expose write tools
